hunt.justification: The rapid adoption of AI agents creates a new impersonation vector that bypasses traditional human-centric behavioral monitoring. Protecting Entra Agent ID integrity ensures that automated workflows are not used as a stealthy exfiltration channel.

meta.name: Entra ID Assistive Agent Impersonation

related.reason: This hunt focuses specifically on assistive agents and Entra Agent ID, not general OAuth application abuse.

meta.analysis: A simple detection rule might catch PowerShell on macOS, but it cannot link that activity back to an Entra ID consent grant and an agentic on-behalf-of flow. This hunt correlates identity-side consent with endpoint-side execution outliers across multiple planes.

stages.name: OAuth Consent for Assistive Agent
observables: Dev Agent Identity Blueprint - NOT FOR PROD

scenario.summary: Attackers exploit Microsoft Entra Assistive Agents by tricking users into granting 'access_agent' scopes via OAuth consent, often using localhost-redirect URIs. This allows the agent to obtain On-Behalf-Of (OBO) tokens to impersonate the user and perform unauthorized actions, such as sending malicious emails via the Microsoft Graph API from attacker-controlled environments using PowerShell.

meta.rationale: Start by identifying all macOS hosts with PowerShell installed. The identity phase should focus on users who have interacted with the Graph CLI application, as this is the primary mechanism for establishing the agent identity scope.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has gained initial access by tricking a user into consenting to an assistive agent blueprint, then used an on-behalf-of flow to execute malicious Graph API actions from a macOS-based PowerShell environment.

hunt.name: Entra ID Assistive Agent Impersonation
hunt.description: This hunt targets the abuse of Microsoft Entra Agent ID, specifically the assistive agent workflow. It follows the attack chain from the initial OAuth consent for the access_agent scope to the final malicious action performed via the Graph API. The hunt identifies high-risk identity sessions and then verifies corresponding endpoint execution. We look for the correlation of unusual Entra ID sign-in patterns, specifically agentic app instances, with endpoint-side PowerShell activity on macOS and corresponding network traffic to Microsoft Graph services.

nodes.label: Find macOS hosts with PowerShell installed

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) = 'powershell' OR LOWER(package_name) = 'pwsh') AND LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%microsoft%'
config.description: Identify the subset of the estate where the malicious execution (PowerShell on macOS) is possible.
config.expected_signal: A list of macOS hostnames with Microsoft PowerShell installed. These hosts represent the potential beachheads for the macOS execution stage.

primitive_config.label: Find macOS hosts with PowerShell installed
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) = 'powershell' OR LOWER(package_name) = 'pwsh') AND LOWER(vendor_name) LIKE '%microsoft%'
primitive_config.expected: A list of macOS hostnames with Microsoft PowerShell installed. These hosts represent the potential beachheads for the macOS execution stage.

config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_name, time FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE (dst_endpoint_name = '{{graph_cli_app_id}}' OR LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) LIKE '%microsoft graph command line%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Locate authentications to the Graph CLI application, which often precedes the local capture of authorization codes.
config.expected_signal: A list of users who have authenticated to the Graph CLI. This is the pool of potentially compromised users who may have granted agent consent.

primitive_config.label: Identify Graph CLI authentication
primitive_config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_name, time FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE (dst_endpoint_name = '{{graph_cli_app_id}}' OR LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) LIKE '%microsoft graph command line%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: A list of users who have authenticated to the Graph CLI. This is the pool of potentially compromised users who may have granted agent consent.

config.content: SELECT dst_endpoint_name, COUNT(DISTINCT actor_user_name) as user_count, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE (LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) LIKE '%blueprint%' OR LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) LIKE '%agent%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY dst_endpoint_name HAVING user_count <= 3
config.description: Stack-count sign-ins to agent blueprints to find rare and suspicious assistive agent activity across the tenant.
config.expected_signal: Rare agent blueprint targets. While some agents are legitimate, those used by only a few users are high-priority for investigation.

primitive_config.label: Detect agentic OBO sign-in patterns
primitive_config.content: SELECT dst_endpoint_name, COUNT(DISTINCT actor_user_name) as user_count, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE (LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) LIKE '%blueprint%' OR LOWER(dst_endpoint_name) LIKE '%agent%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY dst_endpoint_name HAVING user_count <= 3
primitive_config.expected: Rare agent blueprint targets. While some agents are legitimate, those used by only a few users are high-priority for investigation.

config.objective: Identify users who authenticated to Graph CLI and subsequently initiated sessions with rare agent blueprints, potentially via OBO flows.
config.description: Assess whether the Graph CLI authentication and rare agent sign-ins indicate a user impersonation event via assistive agents.
config.expected_signal: A list of high-risk users and agent IDs that require follow-on endpoint investigation.
config.success_criteria: A per-user risk verdict citing the matching sign-in events.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_cmd_line, user_name, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) as host_count, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%pwsh%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%pwsh%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY process_cmd_line HAVING host_count <= 3
config.description: Find outlier PowerShell activity on macOS that may indicate the execution of agent-controlled tasks.
config.expected_signal: PowerShell command lines seen on very few hosts. This filters out common IT scripts and focuses on unique, potentially malicious activity.

nodes.label: Correlate network connections to Microsoft Graph

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, dst_endpoint_hostname, dst_endpoint_ip, time FROM hb_network_connection WHERE (LOWER(dst_endpoint_hostname) LIKE '%graph.microsoft.com%' OR instr(',' || '{{malicious_ips}}' || ',', ',' || dst_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Corroborate that the identified macOS hosts and PowerShell processes are communicating with Graph API or known malicious IPs.
config.expected_signal: Network activity from identified hosts to Graph API endpoints, confirming that the local execution has a corresponding cloud-side impact.
